events.title: Japanese Surrender and Korean Liberation
events.description: Japan surrendered, liberating the Korean Peninsula from 35 years of Japanese colonial rule. However, the peninsula was immediately divided at the 38th parallel, occupied separately by the US and USSR.

events.title: Soviet Occupation of North Korea
events.description: Soviet Red Army entered northern Korean Peninsula, beginning to establish a pro-Soviet regime. USSR installed Kim Il-sung as leader, initiating socialist transformation.

events.title: North Korean Provisional People's Committee Established
events.description: With Soviet support, Kim Il-sung's North Korean Provisional People's Committee was established. Land reform and nationalization policies began.

events.title: Land Reform
events.description: North Korea implemented radical land reform, confiscating landlord land and distributing it to peasants. Simultaneously began industrial nationalization, establishing planned economy.

events.title: DPRK Founded
events.description: With Soviet support, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea was officially established, with Kim Il-sung as Premier (later Chairman), with Pyongyang as capital. The Korean Peninsula was formally split into two nations.

events.title: Sino-DPRK Relations Foundation
events.description: After PRC founding, North Korea established close relations with China. The two countries established 'friendship forged in blood.'

events.title: Korean War Begins
events.description: The Korean People's Army crossed the 38th parallel and launched a major offensive against South Korea, starting the Korean War. North Korea attempted to unify the Korean Peninsula by force.

events.title: Incheon Landing and War Reversal
events.description: UN forces landed at Incheon, cutting off North Korean army's rear, reversing the war. UN forces counterattacked to the Yalu River, North Korean regime in jeopardy.

events.title: Chinese People's Volunteers Enter War
events.description: Chinese People's Volunteers crossed the Yalu River to aid North Korea. China's intervention prevented North Korean collapse, the war entered stalemate.

events.title: Postwar Reconstruction
events.description: With Chinese and Soviet aid, North Korea rapidly rebuilt war-devastated economy. Heavy industry developed rapidly, living standards improved.

events.title: Korean Armistice Signed
events.description: The Korean Armistice Agreement was signed at Panmunjom, ending the war. The division of the Korean Peninsula was solidified along the Demilitarized Zone. The war caused millions of deaths, with North Korean cities nearly leveled.

events.title: Juche Ideology Proposed
events.description: Kim Il-sung proposed 'Juche' ideology, emphasizing self-reliance and independence. Juche ideology became North Korea's guiding ideology, affecting all aspects of politics, economy, and culture.

events.title: Personality Cult Development
events.description: Kim Il-sung personality cult peaked, called 'Great Leader,' 'Sun of the Nation,' 'Marshal.' North Korea became one of the world's most extreme personality cult states.

events.title: Blue House Raid
events.description: North Korean special forces attempted to raid South Korean Blue House (presidential residence) to assassinate President Park Chung-hee. The attempt failed but escalated inter-Korean tensions.

events.title: USS Pueblo Incident
events.description: North Korea captured US intelligence ship USS Pueblo, detaining 83 crew members. After 11 months of negotiations, crew was released. This was US-DPRK major conflict during Cold War.

events.title: July 4 Joint Statement
events.description: North and South Korea issued historic July 4 Joint Statement, agreeing to peaceful reunification principles. Though dialogue didn't last, this was first postwar inter-Korean official agreement.

events.title: Kim Il-sung Becomes President
events.description: North Korea revised constitution, Kim Il-sung became president (previously premier). Kim's power further consolidated, personality cult peaked.

events.title: Kim Jong-il Designated Successor
events.description: At the 6th Workers' Party Congress, Kim Jong-il was publicly designated as Kim Il-sung's successor. North Korea began establishing hereditary regime.

events.title: Rangoon Bombing
events.description: North Korean agents bombed South Korean delegation in Rangoon, Myanmar, killing 17 including several South Korean cabinet ministers. This was major North Korean terrorist attack.

events.title: Kim Jong-il's Power Consolidation
events.description: Kim Jong-il strengthened control over military and party, becoming de facto second-in-command. He began establishing personality cult, preparing for succession from Kim Il-sung.

events.title: Korean Air Flight 858 Bombing
events.description: North Korean agents bombed Korean Air Flight 858, killing all 115 aboard. International community strongly condemned North Korean terrorism.

events.title: Arduous March Famine
events.description: North Korea suffered severe famine, hundreds of thousands or millions died of starvation. Economic collapse and food shortages caused humanitarian disaster.

events.title: North and South Korea Join UN
events.description: North and South Korea simultaneously joined the United Nations. This was important step in international recognition of Korean Peninsula division.

events.title: Basic Agreement on Inter-Korean Relations
events.description: North and South Korea signed Basic Agreement, committing to mutual respect, non-interference, peaceful coexistence. Though not fully implemented, this was important inter-Korean agreement.

events.title: Death of Kim Il-sung
events.description: Kim Il-sung died at age 82. He ruled North Korea for 46 years, called the 'Great Leader' and 'Sun of the Nation.' Kim Jong-il inherited power.

events.title: Agreed Framework Signed
events.description: North Korea and US signed Agreed Framework, North Korea froze nuclear program in exchange for light water reactors and fuel oil. This temporarily eased nuclear crisis.

events.title: Kim Il-sung Becomes Eternal President
events.description: North Korea revised constitution, designating deceased Kim Il-sung as 'Eternal President.' This was unprecedented political arrangement.

events.title: Kim Jong-il Formally Assumes Power
events.description: Kim Jong-il was elected Chairman of National Defense Commission, formally becoming supreme leader. North Korea entered second-generation hereditary rule.

events.title: First Inter-Korean Summit
events.description: Kim Jong-il met with South Korean President Kim Dae-jung in Pyongyang for historic summit. Both sides issued June 15 Joint Declaration, easing inter-Korean relations.

events.title: Second Nuclear Crisis
events.description: US accused North Korea of secret uranium enrichment program, second nuclear crisis erupted. North Korea withdrew from NPT, restarted nuclear program.

events.title: Six-Party Talks
events.description: China hosted Six-Party Talks (China, US, Russia, Japan, North and South Korea) to resolve North Korean nuclear issue. Though some agreements reached, talks ultimately failed.

events.title: Six-Party Talks Agreement
events.description: Six nations reached Joint Statement agreement, with North Korea committing to abandon nuclear programs in exchange for security guarantees and economic aid. However, implementation faced numerous obstacles.

events.title: First Nuclear Test
events.description: North Korea conducted its first nuclear test, claiming successful detonation of a nuclear device. The international community strongly condemned it, and the UN Security Council passed sanctions resolutions. North Korea officially became a nuclear state.

events.title: Second Nuclear Test
events.description: North Korea conducted second nuclear test, advancing nuclear weapons capability. International community imposed stricter sanctions.

events.title: Cheonan Sinking
events.description: South Korean navy corvette Cheonan sank in Yellow Sea, 46 sailors died. International investigation concluded North Korean torpedo attack, North Korea denied.

events.title: Yeonpyeong Island Shelling
events.description: North Korea shelled South Korean Yeonpyeong Island, killing 4. This was most serious inter-Korean military clash since armistice.

events.title: Kim Jong-un Emerges
events.description: Kim Jong-un was publicly revealed as Kim Jong-il's successor, promoted to four-star general. North Korea began third-generation succession preparation.

events.title: Death of Kim Jong-il
events.description: Kim Jong-il died of a heart attack at age 69. His son Kim Jong-un inherited power, and North Korea entered its third generation of hereditary rule.

events.title: Kim Jong-un Formally Assumes Power
events.description: Kim Jong-un became First Secretary of Workers' Party and First Chairman of National Defense Commission. North Korea officially entered third-generation hereditary rule.

events.title: Third Nuclear Test and Purges
events.description: North Korea conducted third nuclear test, international sanctions tightened. Domestically, Kim Jong-un executed powerful uncle Jang Song-thaek, consolidating power through purges.

events.title: Fourth and Fifth Nuclear Tests
events.description: North Korea conducted two nuclear tests in one year, claiming hydrogen bomb capability. International community imposed unprecedented strict sanctions.

events.title: ICBM Tests and Nuclear Brinkmanship
events.description: North Korea tested multiple ICBMs, claiming capability to strike US mainland. Kim Jong-un and Trump exchanged harsh rhetoric, peninsula tensions peaked.

events.title: Sixth Nuclear Test
events.description: North Korea conducted sixth and largest nuclear test, claiming successful hydrogen bomb test. This was North Korea's most powerful nuclear test.

events.title: Singapore US-DPRK Summit
events.description: Kim Jong-un met with US President Trump in Singapore in a historic summit. This was the first meeting between US and North Korean leaders, with both sides signing a joint statement committing to denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula.

events.title: PyeongChang Olympics Diplomatic Thaw
events.description: North Korea sent large delegation to South Korean PyeongChang Olympics, Kim Jong-un's sister Kim Yo-jong attended. This opened new phase of inter-Korean dialogue.

events.title: Panmunjom Inter-Korean Summit
events.description: Kim Jong-un met with South Korean President Moon Jae-in at Panmunjom, signing Panmunjom Declaration. This was third inter-Korean summit, easing peninsula tensions.

events.title: Hanoi US-DPRK Summit
events.description: Kim Jong-un and Trump held second summit in Hanoi, but negotiations collapsed without agreement. Denuclearization dialogue stalled.

events.title: COVID-19 Border Closure
events.description: North Korea completely closed borders to prevent COVID-19, entering unprecedented isolation. Economic difficulties worsened, humanitarian crisis deepened.

events.title: Record Missile Tests
events.description: North Korea conducted record number of missile tests, including ICBMs and submarine-launched ballistic missiles. Kim Jong-un declared North Korea 'irreversible nuclear state.'

events.title: Nuclear Force Policy Law
events.description: North Korea passed Nuclear Force Policy Law, declaring nuclear state status 'irreversible' and stipulating 'automatic' nuclear weapon use under certain circumstances.

events.title: Russia-DPRK Rapprochement
events.description: Kim Jong-un visited Russia, meeting Putin. Western countries suspect North Korea supplying weapons to Russia for Ukraine war, North Korea-Russia relations warmed.

events.title: Abandoning Reconciliation Policy
events.description: Kim Jong-un announced abandoning 'national cooperation' policy, defining South Korea as 'number one hostile state.' Dismantled inter-Korean reconciliation monuments, peninsula tensions escalated.
